I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 25 years. My family has four people, and some work off-farm, so I plan the farm work around what I can handle myself, with extra help at harvest and sowing. We have our own well, so water is not my biggest worry.

It is autumn now. After the maize comes off, I will plant all 5 mu with winter wheat. I always buy improved wheat seed from the county supply store — varieties like Jimai 22 or Luyuan 502 that I have used before and trust. First I plough the stubble under, then I run the rotary tiller to break the soil fine. Before sowing in late October, I spread compound fertilizer as a base. Then I top-dress with urea twice: once when the wheat greens up in spring, and again at jointing. All together that comes to about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphate and potash. I irrigate four times using the well: at sowing, before winter to help the seedlings survive the cold, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray four times — herbicide once, and pesticide for aphids and rust.

As soon as the wheat is harvested in early June, I immediately plant summer maize. There are only a few days between harvest and sowing, so I use no-tillage planting right behind the combine to save time. I only grow hybrid maize — Denghai 605 is what most of us use here, and it gives good yield. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress with urea at the big trumpet stage, about 18 kg nitrogen per mu in total, plus phosphate and potash. I irrigate twice: once after sowing if the soil is dry, and once at silking. I spray three times for stem borers and leaf blight. If the weather is normal, I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat and 550 kg per mu from the maize. This wheat-maize rotation has fed my family for 25 years, so I will stick with it.
